items.q: At the start of the story, the farmer was rich.
Every morning, the farmer gave the goose food and water.

The goose laid two golden eggs every day.
The farmer thought one egg a day was too slow.

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: A poor farmer had a goose that laid one golden egg every day, and he became rich. But he was greedy and wanted all the gold at once. He lost the goose, and there were no more golden eggs.

items.q: What did the farmer do with the first golden egg?
items.model: He took it to town, and a man said it was real gold. He sold it for a lot of money.

items.q: Why was the farmer not satisfied?
items.model: He thought one egg a day was too slow. He wanted all the gold now.

items.q: What happened because of the farmer's greed?
items.model: He lost his wonderful goose, and there were no more golden eggs.

items.q: Why is it sometimes better to have enough than to always want more?

blocks.title: 5. Put in order
blocks.intro: Put the events in the order of the story.
items: The farmer found a bright, shiny egg
The farmer sold the egg in town
The goose laid one golden egg every day
The farmer looked at the empty nest
